scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The upstairs design floor's 172.16.30.x
machines have STOPPED EXISTING for us downstairs -- from my PC5, 172.16.10.x,
every one of them times out, while my own floor is totally fine!! Something
around the big switch that joins the floors must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone look at it and reconnect me to design -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A comprehensive end-to-end audit of the inter-VLAN path between 172.16.10.x (VLAN 10, switch1/mswitch0) and 172.16.30.x (VLAN 30, switch3/mswitch0) reveals no fault. Every component is operating correctly:

All four VLAN-10 hosts (pc5 172.16.10.5, pc6 .6, pc7 .7, pc8 .8) successfully reach all three VLAN-30 hosts (pc12 172.16.30.12, pc13 .13, pc14 .14) with 0% packet loss, including from a completely cold ARP cache. The reverse path also succeeds.

The multilayer switch mswitch0 is correctly performing inter-VLAN routing. It has directly-connected kernel routes for 172.16.10.0/24 (via vlan10, gateway 172.16.10.254) and 172.16.30.0/24 (via vlan30, gateway 172.16.30.254), IP forwarding is enabled, no iptables FORWARD rules exist, and all interface counters show zero errors and zero drops. OSPF adjacency with router16 is FULL. ARP resolution over both VLAN subinterfaces succeeds immediately, even after a full neighbour-table flush.

The access switches switch1 and switch3 are correctly configured: each uses a VLAN subinterface (eth0.10 and eth0.30 respectively) in a dedicated per-VLAN bridge (br_vlan10, br_vlan30) to tag uplink traffic, and the MAC forwarding tables are correctly populated on every hop.

One minor architectural observation: mswitch0's br0 has vlan_filtering disabled (0), causing VLAN-tagged frames to be flooded to all switch uplinks unnecessarily. This is an inefficiency and reduces L2 isolation, but it does not cause any packet loss or routing failure.

The user-reported outage cannot be reproduced in the current lab state. The network is healthy.

The agent's logs show repeated successful inter-VLAN pings (including cold-cache ARP), mswitch0 forwarding enabled, no FORWARD firewall rules, OSPF adjacency, ARP/FDB entries and zero interface errors — all consistent with a healthy inter-VLAN path.
